summary: Larch Mountain lookout, Coeur d'Alene NF: 30-foot pole L-4 tower built 1934, destroyed 1955; a 2025 visit found footings, a chimney and the alidade stand.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1955. A 2025 Idaho Fire Lookouts visit found three of the cement footings, a chimney, a bed frame and debris, and the alidade stand moved nearby.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts describes a hike-in: hot, but not a difficult walk.

events.note: 30-foot pole L-4 tower; both sites date it to 1934
Both sites give 1955 as the year it was destroyed; cause not stated

evidence.supports: Location 10 miles SSW of Clark Fork, Shoshone County
Tower appeared burnt; alidade stand removed and set nearby
evidence.quote: it appeared that the tower was burnt but they removed the alidade stand and placed it nearby

evidence.supports: Top mechanism of the alidade stand still slides
evidence.quote: The top mechanism still slides even!

evidence.supports: Three of the cement footings, chimney, bed frame and debris found
evidence.quote: We also were able to find 3 of the cement footings, the chimney, a bed frame and other assorted piece of debris.

evidence.supports: Hike was hot but not difficult
evidence.quote: while not a difficult hike, the heat made it feel longer than it likely was

notes_for_editor: Only two detailed sources, both giving 1934 build and 1955 destruction. The burnt remark is the visiting writers' impression, so the story says the tower appeared to have burned. No staffing source exists; the Idaho page says none is documented. The brief coordinates (48.01733, -116.27380) should be checked against the firelookout.com location (10 miles SSW of Clark Fork) on a map; by a rough check they look closer to Clark Fork than that. No image URL captured. Neither page defines the term alidade, so the story no longer glosses it; add a sourced definition if the term needs one.
